summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV (CD4 22, high viral load), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic post-herpetic neuralgia presented with acute lightheadedness, weakness, and nausea following a dialysis session. She was unable to rise from the couch and required emergency assistance. Initial concerns included sepsis due to her immunocompromised state, but she remained afebrile with no infectious source identified; chest imaging was clear and blood cultures showed no growth. Her symptoms were attributed to pregabalin (Lyrica), started two days prior for neuropathic pain, which she had previously not tolerated in the form of gabapentin. Lyrica was discontinued, IV fluids were given for hypotension, and empiric antibiotics were stopped after 24 hours. She improved clinically, tolerated initiation of low-dose duloxetine post-dialysis for pain, and was discharged home with supportive services, medication reconciliation, and follow-up plans for HIV treatment reinitiation and psychiatric evaluation.
